questions.q: Fisher’s quantity theory is explained by his famous equation given as .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is MV = PT. Key Points

• Fisher's quantity theory:-

• It​ is a monetary theory that explains the relationship between money supply, velocity of money, price level, and output.

• The famous equation given by Fisher is MV = PT, where M is the money supply, V is the velocity of money, P is the price level, and T is the level of transactions.

• The equation suggests that an increase in the money supply (M) will lead to an increase in the price level (P), assuming that the velocity of money (V) and the level of transactions (T) are constant.

• The theory also implies that changes in the money supply have a direct impact on inflation, as an increase in the money supply leads to an increase in the price level, which in turn reduces the purchasing power of money.

Additional Information

• The quantity theory of money has been subject to criticism over the years, with some economists arguing that it oversimplifies the complex dynamics of the economy.

• One of the criticisms is that the velocity of money is not constant and can vary significantly over time, making it difficult to predict the impact of changes in the money supply on the price level.

• Another criticism is that the theory assumes that the level of transactions is fixed, which is not always the case as it can be influenced by a variety of factors such as technology, demographics, and government policies.

questions.q: Select the FALSE statement from the given options.
options: Baikal rocks are formed from the dissolved materials that precipitate from the solution.
The sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition and subsequent cementation of that material within bodies of water and at the surface of the earth.
Metamorphic rocks may be formed simply by being deep beneath the Earth’s surface, subjected to high temperatures and the great pressure of the rock layers above it.
Igneous rock is formed through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Baikal rocks are formed from the dissolved materials that precipitate from the solution. Key Points

• Baikal rocks are actually formed from the solidification of magma or lava, not from dissolved materials that precipitate from the solution. -

• Sedimentary rocks are indeed formed by the deposition and subsequent cementation of material within bodies of water and at the surface of the earth.

• Metamorphic rocks are formed by the alteration of existing rock types through heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids.

• Igneous rocks are indeed formed through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.

Additional Information

• Baikal rocks refer to the rocks found in the Baikal Rift Zone, a region of active tectonic activity in Russia.

• Sedimentary rocks are the most common type of rock on Earth and include types such as sandstone, limestone, and shale.
